en: The Sun is roughly 109 times wider than Earth, meaning about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside its massive volume.
Jupiter is the largest planet, with a diameter of 139,820 kilometers, making it about 11 times wider than Earth.
The Moon orbits at an average distance of 384,400 kilometers, meaning roughly 30 Earths could fit in that space.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our solar system, located about 4.24 light-years, or 40 trillion kilometers, away.
The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California, in 1913.
The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometers, making it larger than all of Earth's landmasses combined.
On the Mohs hardness scale, diamond is the hardest natural mineral at 10, while talc is the softest at 1.
Clay soil particles are the smallest at under 0.002 millimeters, whereas sand particles are the largest at up to 2.0 millimeters.
The strongest earthquake ever recorded was the 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile, which measured a massive 9.5 magnitude.
Mauna Kea in Hawaii is the tallest volcano on Earth, measuring 10,210 meters from its underwater base to its peak.
The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's, so a 60-kilogram student would weigh only 10 kilograms there.
Glaciers and ice caps hold about 68.7 percent of Earth's fresh water, with most of it locked in Antarctica.
